items.q: The serum calcium threshold above which hypercalcemia evaluation should begin (mg/dl) is:
items.exp: Adjusted Ca 8.6–10.3 mg/dl; hypercalcemia >10.5 mg/dl starts evaluation. (Book p877)
0.25 mmol = 0.5 meq/l = 1 mg/dl of calcium. (Book p877)

items.q: Match shares — 1) Parathyroid gland dependent  2) Vit-D related … A) 80%  B) 20%
The most common cause of hypercalcemia overall is:
items.exp: Primary hyperparathyroidism is m/c overall. (Book p877)

items.q: Primary parathyroid adenomas (85%) most commonly arise in the:
Hyperplasia associations — 1) MEN  2) MEON … A) CDC73 (carcinoma)  B) Type 1 > Type 2A
items.exp: MEN type 1 > type 2A; MEON: CDC73 (carcinoma); also sporadic. (Book p877)

opts: AD CaSR loss-of-function mutation with low 24 hr urine calcium
AD CaSR gain-of-function mutation with high urine calcium
AR CaSR loss-of-function mutation with high urine calcium
X-linked CaSR loss-of-function with normal urine calcium
items.exp: FHH: AD, CaSR loss of mutation, low 24 hr urine calcium. (Book p877)

items.q: PTHrP-dependent hypercalcemia is classically associated with:
opts: Squamous cell carcinoma of lung, head and neck
items.exp: PTHrP (↓↓): squamous cell carcinoma lung, head and neck. (Book p877)

items.q: Miscellaneous ENDOCRINE causes listed are Addison's disease, pheochromocytoma and thyrotoxicosis. Pick the ODD ONE OUT:
items.exp: Endocrine: Addison's, pheochromocytoma, thyrotoxicosis — Cushing's is not listed. (Book p877)

items.q: Osteolytic hypercalcemia causes listed are Ca breast (m/c), Ca lung and multiple myeloma. Pick the ODD ONE OUT:
items.exp: Osteolytic: breast (m/c), lung, myeloma — prostate not listed. (Book p877)

items.q: ‘Thiazide-induced hypercalcemia and milk-alkali syndrome are miscellaneous causes of hypercalcemia.’
items.exp: Miscellaneous includes milk-alkali syndrome and thiazide-induced. (Book p877)
